Gel can be easier to apply and a bit less messy, still liquid is what AMD uses. Many suggest starting with DMSO Store non-diluted liquid roll-on on clean, dry skin to get a feel for the product.

To keep this post shorter, please go here and scroll down to learn how to patch test skin, and for specifics on HOW to dilute and use DMSO both topically and orally. A Midwestern Doctor (the expert) has kept this information behind a paywall.

Important Notes on Diluting, Measuring, and Safe for DMSO Materials

• Use Reverse Osmosis water or distilled water to dilute DMSO to required %.  Calculator

• To make these recipes, you will need a 50ml amber glass dropper bottle and small marked measuring glass for measuring in millileters (mL) as in the recipes below. Since you’re working with DMSO, to make combination recipes in a compatible roller ball, this PP (polypropylene) roller ball applicator is the right call, and it is not so small that you need to refill it often.

• When mixing and storing, remember glass is non-reactive and does not give off toxins like plastics can. Not all plastics are incompatible with DMSO. DMSO is compatible with plastics such as PETE, HDPE, LDPE, and polypropylene #5 (PP) without the risk of contamination or reactivity. Avoid application with synthetic fragrances, as DMSO also increases absorption of unwanted substances into the body.

If your storage container leaches chemicals into the DMSO, those contaminants come with it. Even the label adhesive on your bottle (or Sharpie ink) can leach into you, so I hold and apply the roller bottle with 1 dry hand and massage in with the other. 

• After massaging in with fingertips, wash hands well with just plain water or only VERY basic soap (like Bronner’s Castile) before moving onto other things which could possibly draw in contaminants. PS. this soap has become my facial soap because of it’s pure ingredients.

23 Fabulous Synergistic Recipes:

1. Burn Soothing Gel

This gel reduces pain, prevents infection, and promotes skin repair in minor burns. Lavender oil soothes irritation, while aloe vera hydrates the skin. Don’t use on open wounds or third-degree burns. Ingredients: 1 small glass jar with lid, 2-3 tablespoons 50% DMSO solution, 2 tablespoons aloe vera gel with no preservatives, 1 teaspoon silver gel, 5 drops lavender essential oil. Instructions: Mix DMSO solution with aloe and lavender oil. Gently mix before each use and gently apply to minor burns. Avoiding rubbing and leave on until absorbed. Apply 2-3 times daily as needed.

This chest rub aids in relieving congestion and supporting respiratory health. Use as needed during colds or respiratory discomfort. Avoid the eyes. Ingredients: 50 mL glass jar, 30 mL 99.99% pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, 10 mL non-refined virgin coconut oil, 10 mL eucalyptus essential oil, 2 drops peppermint essential oil. Instructions: Melt coconut oil over very low heat and mix in DMSO and essential oils. Transfer to a small glass jar and it will thicken as it cools. Apply a small amount to the chest, massaging gently.

This topical solution improves blood flow and shrinks/reduces the appearance of varicose veins. Apply daily, focusing on affected areas.  Ingredients: this refillable DMSO-approved (polypropylene) roller bottle, 30 mL 99.995% pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, 10 mL distilled water to dilute, 5 mL witch hazel, 5 drops lavender and 5 drops helichrysum essential oils. Instructions: Combine all ingredients  and replace the refillable roller top, shaking gently to blend before use. Roll onto worst areas and gently massage into the skin. Use twice daily for optimal results. Let dry 10-20 minutes.

This cream promotes scar healing by softening tissue, reducing discoloration, and stimulating collagen production. Vitamin E and calendula oil enhance skin repair and hydration. Use for at least four weeks for noticeable improvements. Ingredients: 4 teaspoons of DMSO diluted to 70% solution, 1 teaspoon of this natural (not synthetic) vitamin E oil, and 1 teaspoon organic calendula oil. May add 3 pillules of thiosinaminum 6 and let dissolve (read about this amazing homeopathic here). Instructions: Blend ingredients thoroughly in a small glass container. Apply the cream to scars twice daily, massaging it gently into the skin.

This gel helps reduce inflammation, ease joint stiffness, and promote circulation in affected areas.  Ingredients: 2 tablespoons 70% DMSO gel, 2 tablespoons Aloe vera gel (preservative-free), 15 drops wintergreen essential oil, and 1 teaspoon arnica oil.  Instructions: Mix everything thoroughly in a small glass bowl. Massage the gel to the affected joint twice daily. Store any remaining mixture in a glass airtight container away from light. Use consistently for several weeks for best results.

This solution targets acne by reducing inflammation, fighting bacteria, and promoting skin healing. Tea tree oil acts as a natural antimicrobial agent, while aloe vera soothes irritated skin. Do a patch skin test first. Discontinue use if irritation occurs. Ingredients: 4-5 teaspoons of 40% DMSO solution, 5 drops tea tree essential oil, 2 teaspoons aloe vera juice. Instructions: Mix together in a small dish. Dab the mixture onto acne-prone areas using a cotton swab using clean hands. Avoid the temptation to squeeze your face. Allow it to completely dry before applying any other products. Apply twice daily for best results.

This spray is designed to improve circulation and ease the discomfort of restless leg syndrome, particularly during the evening when symptoms often worsen, providing a calming effect. Ingredients: this refillable 50 mL DMSO-approved (polypropylene) roller bottle, ~42 mL 70% DMSO solution, 3 tablespoons magnesium oil, 5 drops lavender essential oil. Instructions: Add the ingredients into a roller ball bottle. Shake first and apply evenly over clean legs and feet, ensuring full coverage. Gently massage the solution into the skin until fully absorbed. Allow it to dry before lying down or covering with bedding. Use nightly before bed.

This treatment alleviates pain, reduces swelling, and accelerates the healing of cold sores. Lemon balm oil has antiviral properties, while colloidal silver aids in infection control. Avoid use on areas other than cold sores, and always use clean tools to apply. Ingredients: 2 teaspoons 50% DMSO solution, 5 drops lemon balm [melissa officianalis] essential oil. Since the EO is very expensive, you can substitute 30 drops lemon balm [melissa officianalis] tincture , and 1 teaspoon colloidal silver. Instructions: Mix all together in a small container. Apply directly to cold sores using a cotton swab. Repeat 3-4 times daily.

This healing sinus rinse helps manage infections, polyps, and general inflammation with a gentle 5–10% DMSO concentration. Avoid usage if the nasal lining is raw or bleeding. Frequent use may alleviate chronic issues, but always consult a specialist for severe conditions. Ingredients: 12 mL 99.995 percent pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, a ceramic Neti pot, 8 ounces distilled water, ¼ teaspoon neti salt or noniodized sea salt, ½ teaspoon 20 ppm colloidal silver, ½ teaspoon preservative-free aloe vera juice (optional). Instructions: Dissolve salt in lukewarm distilled water. Mix in DMSO and colloidal silver, stirring gently. Add aloe vera gel juice if the solution stings. 10. Soothing Foot Bath in a stainless or #5 plastic (polypropylene) foot tub

This bath promotes detoxification and reduces inflammation by drawing out toxins through the feet. Baking soda neutralizes acidity, while Epsom salts relax muscles. Use 1-2 times weekly for overall wellness.  Ingredients: ½ cup DMSO (30% solution), 1 cup Epsom salts, 1 tablespoon baking soda, 3 drops tea tree essential oil. Use warm water. Instructions: Dissolve Epsom salts and baking soda in warm water in a stainless steel or porcelain (not run of the mill plastic or aluminum) foot basin. Add the DMSO solution. Soak feet for 20-30 minutes and pat dry.

This serum reduces fine lines and wrinkles by boosting skin hydration and collagen production. DMSO enhances the penetration of vitamin E, castor oil, and rosehip oil to deeper cell layers almost like Botox. Apply nightly to clean skin. Test a small area first for sensitivity. Ingredients: 1 teaspoon 40% DMSO solution, 1 teaspoon vitamin E oil, 1 teaspoon rosehip oil. Instructions: Mix all ingredients in a small container. Ingredients: 50 mL glass dropper bottle, 44 mL 99.995% pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, 1 mL Lugol’s 2% iodine or 10% povidone-iodine, 10 drops tea tree essential oil. This 10% DMSO and colloidal silver solution addresses ear infections, inflammation, and discomfort. Use for one week, continuing treatment for a few days after symptoms subside to prevent recurrence. Do not use if the eardrum is ruptured or if fluid leakage persists without medical advice. Ingredients: 50 mL glass dropper bottle, 45 mL colloidal silver, 5 mL 99.995 percent pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, and 10 drops mullein garlic oil. Instructions: Combine in the new dropper bottle. Shake gently and allow the exothermic (heat) reaction to complete then add the mullein oil. Apply 1–2 drops in each ear once or twice daily for a week. 18. Mouthwash

This mouthwash addresses gum disease and minor oral infections. Ingredients: 5 mL 99.995% pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, 5 mL 3% food-grade hydrogen peroxide, 10-12 mL distilled water or preservative-free aloe vera gel or juice. Instructions: Mix all ingredients in a clean container. Swish twice daily, but don’t swallow it. Rinse thoroughly with water after use.

If you have a patient that cannot swallow, this topical blend provides essential vitamins and minerals transdermally to support overall health. Apply daily or as needed, but monitor skin reactions to ensure compatibility. Not for internal use. Ingredients: 50 mL glass dropper bottle, 40 mL 99.995% pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, 10mL ionic trace mineral drops, 1 mL magnesium oil, 2 drops Lugol’s 2% iodine or povidone-iodine, powder from 1/2 whole food capsule methylated B-complex vitamin, 10 mL preservative-free aloe vera gel or juice, and powder from ½ capsule whole food vitamin C. Instructions: Using a funnel, add all ingredients to the bottle. Shake well to combine. With whole food caps, it may have slight greenish tint. Apply 3–5 mL to targeted areas of the body once or twice daily. Store in a cool, dark place and replace the mixture after six months.

20. Arthritis Joint Relief Rub

This rub alleviates joint and inflammation caused by arthritis. Its combination of DMSO, turmeric, and ginger penetrates deeply to reduce discomfort. Ingredients: 50 mL glass jar, 30 mL 99.995% pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, 10 mL distilled water to dilute, 2 teaspoons turmeric tincture, 1 teaspoon ginger powder or tincture, 1/2 teaspoon arnica oil, 1 teaspoon virgin (not refined) coconut oil. Instructions: Mix all into a paste. Slowly add DMSO and distilled water, stirring continuously to blend. Apply a small amount over the affected joint, massaging gently. Leave for 15–20 minutes, then wipe away residue with a damp cloth. Use twice daily for best results.

21. Stretch Mark Reduction Blend

This formula targets stretch marks, improving skin elasticity and appearance. Apply daily for several weeks to see visible results. Do not use on irritated or broken skin. Ingredients: 50 mL glass bottle with dropper 20 mL 99.995% pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, 10 mL vitamin E oil, 10 mL rosehip oil, 10 mL aloe vera gel/ juice. Instructions: Combine all ingredients in the bottle and shake to mix thoroughly. Apply a few drops to stretch marks, massaging gently into the skin. Allow the blend to absorb fully.

22. Healing Salve for Cracked Heels

This rich salve heals cracked heels, moisturizing and softening the skin. Apply nightly for best results. Avoid using on infected skin. Ingredients: 50 mL glass jar, 20 mL 99.995% pharmaceutical-grade DMSO, 15 mL coconut oil, 10 mL shea butter, 5 mL vitamin E oil. Instructions: Melt coconut oil and shea butter together over low heat. Stir in vitamin E oil and DMSO. Allow to cool before transferring to the jar. Massage into clean heels and wear old, clean cotton socks overnight.

23. Muscle Recovery Roll- On

This roll-on supports muscle recovery after work outs or overuse by increasing circulation, relaxing tense muscles, and replenishing magnesium levels, which are often depleted during intense activity. Peppermint oil provides a cooling sensation to relieve soreness. Ingredients: this refillable 50 mL DMSO-approved (polypropylene) roller bottle, 50% DMSO solution, 3 tablespoons magnesium oil, 5 drops peppermint essential oil, 5 drops lavender essential oil. Instructions: Add the ingredients into a roller ball bottle. Shake well before use. Wipe off sweat (as it contains toxins the body just released) before applying. Roll on and gently massage until absorbed.

For the preparedness-minded, these small yet impactful uses embody the spirit of natural self-care. You can print out these recipes and keep them handy for minimal effort and maximum efficacy.

Despite its numerous benefits, DMSO remains underutilized and often misunderstood. Regulatory agencies, influenced by pharmaceutical interests, have limited public access to DMSO and its full healing potential until recently.

articles.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.content:
U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

Hackers aligned with ShinyHunters have claimed credit for dozens of major data breaches since 2019, when the group was primarily operated by cybercriminals living in France. As those original members were arrested or jailed one by one, control over the ShinyHunters brand eventually passed to “Rey,” identified last year as a teenage hacker from Amman, Jordan. According to the FBI, ShinyHunters has extorted more than $70 million from victims so far this year.

In late September, ShinyHunters hacked the FBI recruitment website fbijobs.gov and taunted the agency by threatening to publish the stolen files, which reportedly included medical and psychological records, Social Security numbers and home addresses, and information about each employee’s unit and specialization.

The FBI jobs site hack has prompted the agency to move with uncommon speed to arrest, detain and question people who had any communications with Rey or other ShinyHunters suspects. Reuters reported on October 3 that Rey had been detained by Jordanian authorities and was cooperating with the FBI.

Rey was able to assume control over the hacking group because one of its alleged senior members had just been nabbed. On the evening of September 15, 2026, authorities in the Netherlands arrested convicted hacker and ShinyHunters suspect Pepijn van der Stap. Dutch police reportedly used flash-bang grenades in an effort to stun and apprehend Van der Stap as he was logged in to various online accounts.

According to a source close to the investigation, the authorities arrested Van der Stap while he was using his Signal instant messaging account, which allowed them to read recent communications with frequent contacts — including ransomware negotiators based in Canada and the United States.

Multiple sources with knowledge of the matter told KrebsOnSecurity that Van der Stap’s messages were the key to unraveling a murder-for-hire plot that emerged immediately following his arrest. The Dutch news outlet RTL reported last month the two murders were allegedly to be committed abroad, and that there are indications Van der Stap gave the order for the attacks (there is no indication those orders were ever carried out).

On October 9, KrebsOnSecurity broke the news that the FBI arrested a 54-year-old Canadian cybersecurity executive named Edward Dubrovsky in connection with the ShinyHunters investigation. Dubrovsky, who recently published a book on handling cyber extortion that recommended always engaging with the hackers, was charged with threatening to disclose stolen or hacked data and interfering with interstate commerce through extortion, according to court records. Politico reports prosecutors have asked that Dubrovsky remain in custody pending trial, and that records related to his case remain under seal.

A source close to the investigation told KrebsOnSecurity that Van der Stap’s Signal messages showed he had frequent conversations with Mr. Dubrovsky and with at least one executive at a large U.S.-based consulting firm, and that these executives often knew the details about new ShinyHunters victims before the victims themselves had even learned of the breach.

That source shared another potentially explosive finding by federal investigators: the Dutch hacker’s chats showed Mr. Dubrovsky knew ShinyHunters had stolen highly sensitive data from FBI servers, and that he never informed the bureau of the data breach prior to ShinyHunters threatening on Twitter/X to publish the agency’s deeply personal personnel files.

SHINYWIRE

KrebsOnSecurity has learned from two sources close to the ShinyHunters probe that FBI investigators believe at least one executive at a U.S.-based consulting firm played an active role in operating the now-defunct ShinyHunters victim extortion website “shinywire[.]com.” KrebsOnSecurity is not naming the U.S. company or the suspected executive(s) for now because they have not yet been charged with a crime, but it is a prestigious firm with more than 1,000 associates.

A section of the homepage for the now-defunct Shinywire website.

The Shinywire website was active from approximately May 3, 2026 until October 16 and had entries for nearly 100 organizations hacked by ShinyHunters. Each entry urged victims to engage with the cybercrime group and discuss terms for payment. The pages also included samples of stolen files and promised those files would be published online if the victim ignored their demands.

The following screenshot shows a cached portion of the Shinywire extortion page for Intuitive Surgical, an American medical technology company that was breached in March 2026 after an employee fell for a targeted phishing email.

The Shinywire website, as indexed by urlscan.io. This listing is an extortion demand targeting Intuitive Surgical, an American medical technology company breached in March 2026 by a targeted phishing email attack that compromised an employee’s credentials.

Victim organizations that refused to engage or negotiate after seven days would find all of their stolen data published on the ShinyHunters victim shaming blog (a website that is only reachable via the anonymity network Tor).

In a story published October 15, The Globe and Mail wrote that a few months before Edward Dubrovsky was arrested by the FBI, the Canadian cybersecurity executive alleged in court documents he had become collateral damage in a campaign by a former business partner to “destroy” another industry executive.

The story noted that Dubrovsky filed the lawsuit in Ontario this year against Daniel Tobok, the former chief executive of Cypfer, a cybersecurity firm founded in Toronto with offices in the U.S., Britain, the Netherlands, the United Arab Emirates, and Mexico. The two first became business partners in 2017 and later developed Cypfer together, where Mr. Dubrovsky was a managing partner and chief operating officer. But by 2024, the two had a falling out, with Dubrovsky accusing Tobok of gradually excluding him from business matters and making “increasingly capricious business decisions.”

Mr. Tobok reportedly denied the allegations and filed a counterclaim, accusing Mr. Dubrovsky of accessing confidential information and unfairly competing with Cypfer through work at another firm called CyberSteward Inc. He also said Mr. Dubrovsky has misrepresented himself as a Cypfer founder, and is not a shareholder.

GHOSTBYTE

According to interviews with several former colleagues of Mr. Tobok, as far back as eight years ago he was known to ransomware purveyors by a particular nickname: Ghostbyte. In 2018, a Canadian company was hacked by Dharma, a prolific Russian-language ransomware affiliate program that first surfaced in 2016. The victim company told the Dharma ransomware representative they were leaning toward paying because some of the files were unrecoverable after being locked, but that they needed a better guarantee that Dharma would keep their word if paid.

A redacted copy of the Dharma rep’s reply is pictured below, and it shows the ransomware group urged the victim to contact a person at a Canadian IT firm that helps companies seeking such guarantees. The Dharma rep recommended the victim contact the email address ghostbyte@tutanota.com.

“If you want guarantees, you can write to the IT company,” the Dharma reply advised. “Take the phone and negotiate with them. This IT company often solves such problems in Canada. You can contact them and sign a contract for services. You’ll still have to pay.”

An email reply from the Dharma ransomware group to a victim, recommending they contact an email address that is connected to Mr. Tobok.

It’s unclear if Mr. Tobok ever used that Ghostbyte address offered by the Dharma representative, and he has not responded to multiple requests for comment. However, the breach tracking service Constella Intelligence finds an email address Mr. Tobok has frequently used — dtobok@me.com — is associated with two online accounts where the chosen username was “ghostbyte,” including a Snapchat account.

Incidentally, Constella also finds the Dharma rep’s email address luckygoodlucky@tuta.io is associated with a cryptocurrency address that processed 38 transactions totaling 43 bitcoin, ~$3.5 million at today’s value (the most recent transaction for this wallet is dated February 2019).

In a statement shared on October 14, Cypfer said the company’s business does not include making or facilitating ransomware payments, and that Cypfer learned of Dubrovsky’s arrest when the news first broke in the media.

“We had no prior knowledge of Mr. Dubrovsky’s arrest,” a spokesperson told KrebsOnSecurity via email. “CYPFER has not received any outreach from law enforcement and, to our knowledge, is not the target of any law enforcement investigation.”

The statement said CyberSteward and Cypfer are separate companies with no officers, directors or employees in common, and that Cypfer was recently acquired by the Apros Group, a holding company led by Jason Hogg, a former FBI special agent and former CEO of Aon Cyber Solutions Group. In 2020, Aon aquired Cytelligence, a security consulting firm where Mr. Tobok was founder and CEO and Mr. Dubrovsky was a managing partner.

CONFLICTING INTERESTS

It is not illegal in the United States to pay hackers for an encryption key to unlock servers infected with ransomware, or in exchange for a promise to delete any stolen files and refrain from publishing them online. While victim organizations can land in legal hot water if they pay a ransom to a group that is sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury Department, ShinyHunters is not among the ransomware groups currently sanctioned by the United States or by any other government.

Experts say ransomware victims are typically directed by their insurance provider to work with a specific incident response firm. But not all cyber forensics and breach response companies will agree to facilitate payments to ransomware groups on behalf of their clients. As a result, once victim firms make a decision to pay, the firms that eschew rewarding extortionists are invariably replaced by companies that have no such qualms.

In December 2024, ShinyHunters began extorting the education technology company PowerSchool, stealing private information on 62 million students and 9.5 million teachers in the U.S. and Canada. PowerSchool reportedly paid a $2.85 million ransom demand, and a “frequently asked questions” statement (PDF) about the breach says PowerSchool was assisted in that effort by CyberSteward (ShinyHunters affiliate Matthew Lane, 20, of Sterling, Mass., was sentenced in November 2025 to four years in prison for his admitted role in the PowerSchool hack).

But that ransom payment did not stop future extortion attempts using the same stolen data. By May 2025, individual school districts were reportedly receiving separate ransom demands using samples of the same stolen files. While nobody has alleged ShinyHunters was behind the second wave of extortion against PowerSchool users, the incident drives home the reality that there is no technical way to verify the threat actors have deleted the stolen data as promised, or prevent others from abusing the same records.

A number of leading cyber incident response firms, including Coveware and Unit 221B, have consistently warned victims against paying ShinyHunters, noting that “destroyed” victim data is often kept, resold or used to extort the company’s clients directly later on.

The FBI echoed those sentiments in an alert on May 15, 2026 advising victims against paying the ShinyHunters group. Meanwhile, ShinyHunters members have been harassing and threatening employees at Coveware and Unit 221B for offering this advice.

The following screenshots show just how annoyed the ShinyHunters leaders were with Coveware’s relentless advice against paying the group. The first image is from a conversation on May 6, 2026 that took place between the group’s main account on Telegram and a co-conspirator. In that chat, snippets of which were shared with KrebsOnSecurity by a trusted source, ShinyHunters complained that Coveware was harming the group’s payment rates.

The operator of the ShinyHunters account on Telegram speaking privately with a co-conspirator and complaining that Coveware was harming their business.

“Go on my website, majority of those companies would’ve paid if it weren’t for Coveware giving them misinformation,” the ShinyHunters account wrote. “Someone (100% Coveware) is going out of their way to make sure i am not paid.”

In another conversation on April 11, 2026, the ShinyHunters Telegram account privately said they were trying to “eliminate the problem,” which they said was Coveware. Coveware declined to comment for this story.

“I’m sure the company will pay but in this specific case I am aware of Coveware and their involvement, and I’ve probably been not getting a lot of other negotiations mostly likely because Coveware keeps getting involved,” the ShinyHunters account bemoaned.

The operator of the ShinyHunters account on Telegram telling a co-conspirator they were “trying to eliminate the problem,” which they identified as Coveware advising victims not to pay the cybercrime group.

Mark Camillo is chief executive at CyberAcuView, an industry group founded in 2021 by a consortium of major cyber insurance carriers. Camillo said some firms charge a flat retainer fee, while those that specialize in helping companies negotiate a ransom payment tend to charge a percentage of the total ransom amount paid.

That latter dynamic, he said, is an inherent conflict of interest, as the negotiator has every incentive to make things more favorable to the attackers because they are financially incentivized to negotiate and pay out, and to not negotiate down on the price.

“It has come to the industry’s attention that many of the ransomware payers charge a percentage of the final payment which may or may not be disclosed,” Camillo said. “This makes no sense if they are also the negotiator. There needs to be more transparency in the process as no one in the ecosystem should be profiting purely on the size of the ransomware transaction or payment itself.”

Camillo said the firms doing this work would argue the fees are needed because there may be unexpectedly higher costs to secure larger quantities of cryptocurrency or more risk carrying the float, and because cryptocurrency exchanges may charge higher fees for high risk transactions.

“There definitely needs to be more visibility around the transaction and clarity on the increasing value of the crypto and the exchange’s percent in the transaction to get to the bottom of this and remove any misaligned incentives,” he said.

In recent months, the U.S. Department of Justice has prosecuted a number of ransomware negotiators alleged to have conspired with cybercriminals to defraud their clients. On October 7, the DOJ charged MonsterCloud CEO Zohar Pinhasi, 50, with wire fraud and conspiracy for allegedly charging customers to remediate ransomware attacks without paying the hackers. According to charging documents, Pinhasi secretly went behind his customers’ backs and paid hackers anyway, paying ransomware groups $8 million while charging customers $19 million.

In July, Angelo Martino, a 41-year-old ransomware negotiator from Land O’Lakes, Florida, was sentenced to 70 months in prison for conspiring with the Blackcat/ALPHV ransomware group to extort multiple victims. According to the DOJ, Martino was paid by BlackCat attackers to provide confidential information about the negotiating position and strategy of his employer’s clients and enable the ransomware actors to maximize the ransoms paid by the victims.

articles.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
articles.content:
The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

Heleket’s support agent on Telegram claims, despite all evidence to the contrary, that it is not affiliated with Cryptomus. Image: Richard Sanders.

On October 8, the U.K. issued sanctions (PDF) against Cryptomus — previously known as Certa Payments and Xeltox Enterprises — for processing payments that benefit the Russian government and its financial institutions. The sanctions freeze any Cryptomus assets at U.K. banks, and bar British companies from offering it any business, virtual or otherwise. Also targeted in these sanctions were the virtual payment platforms VexPay, TokenSpot, and the Tsunami Payments service.

As explained in our December 2024 investigation, “How Cryptocurrency Turns to Cash in Russian Banks,” Cryptomus has been a key payment processor for dozens of Russian cryptocurrency exchanges and websites hawking cybercrime services. The company has changed its name several times since emerging in 2022, most recently to “Heleket” last year after Canada levied a record CAD $176 million fine against the platform for anti-money laundering violations.

The blockchain data-crunching firm Chainalysis said the U.K. sanctions target the broader infrastructure supporting Russia’s wartime economy.

“Cryptomus and Heleket have emerged as major payment hubs for illicit activity,” Chainalysis wrote in an October 8 blog post. “Together, these services received more illicit funds across tracked categories than the mixers in our dataset and the number of illicit counterparties surged to more than 900 in a single month in late 2025.”

The Cryptomus support bot on Telegram, responding on Oct. 8 to an inquiry by saying the platform was suddenly unable to process transactions.

In April 2026, the blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs found Cryptomus had processed more than $7 billion in transactions since its inception in 2022, including transactions associated with child sexual abuse material vendors, terrorist financing networks, and human trafficking operations.

TRM noted that Cryptomus’s transaction volume cratered after the platform instituted new “know your customer” or KYC rules, and that the cryptocurrency platform responded to the Canadian fines by launching Heleket as a parallel service that continued to offer no-KYC payment processing.

Richard Sanders is a blockchain analyst and investigator who spent months mapping out Cryptomus’s payment infrastructure and transacting with its customers. Sanders said the U.K. sanctions on Cryptomus are important because Canada’s fine against the platform was ultimately unenforceable and uncollectible.

“A fine doesn’t stop a cryptocurrency payment processor from processing payments,” Sanders wrote on LinkedIn. “Sanctions kill the operation. The distinction matters.”

As our 2024 investigation noted, Cryptomus shared a Vancouver address with dozens of other foreign currency dealers and money transfer businesses — none of which appeared to be physically located there. Following the CAD $176 million fine for alleged money laundering violations, Cryptomus appealed the penalty, launched Heleket as a parallel service, and kept on processing large volumes of sketchy transactions, Sanders said.

Sanders said the sanctions also are notable because they are the first known instance of a “Five Eyes” country (referring to the Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the U.K. and the U.S.) sanctioning a cryptocurrency operation incorporated in another Five Eyes jurisdiction.

Where do entities like Cryptomus and Heleket derive their authority to offer international financial services? The answer appears to involve fake financial institutions overseen by a phony regulatory body positioned in a country that is not widely recognized as a sovereign nation.

Our 2024 investigation found the sole shareholder of Cryptomus’s parent company Certa Payments was a 25-year-old Ukrainian woman who also headed several other firms, including the WS Management and Advisory Corporation, which bills itself as the regulatory body that exclusively oversees licenses for cryptocurrency, foreign exchange and online gaming businesses incorporated in the disputed region in northwest Africa known as the Western Sahara.

That entity’s website — crasadr.com — says it assists applicants with bank setup and formation, online gaming licenses, and the creation and licensing of foreign exchange brokers. One of Certa Payments’ former sites — certa[.]website — also shared a server with 12 other domains, including rasd-state[.]ws, a website for the Central Reserve Authority of the Western Sahara.

The website crasadr dot com, the official website of the Central Reserve Authority of Western Sahara, which lists the entities awarded licenses for cryptocurrencies, gaming and foreign exchange services.

articles.title: Keadilan TIDAK BISA DIBELI dengan AMAL.
articles.content:
Bayangkan pemilik dapur MBG korupsi 10M, hakim melepaskan orang tersebut karena dia memberikan santunan kepada 100 orang anak Yatim-Piatu. Adilkah?

Seseorang berhutang 150 jt kepada orang lain, lalu berkata “Saya tidak membayar hutang, tapi kan saya sering berbuat baik kepada orang lain”. Adilkah?

Lalu pikirkan seorang rohaniawan melakukan perzinahan dan dosa-dosa lainnya, lalu dia berpuasa selama sebulan. Menurut ajarannya puasanya ini dapat menghapus semua dosa-dosanya. Setelah puasa dia kembali suci seperti bayi. Adilkah? Adilkah? Adilkah? 🤔

Sang yang maha adil tidak mungkin tidak adil, karena Dialah KEADILAN. Keadilan menuntut setiap dosa/kejahatan HARUS dihukum. Jika dosa/kejahatan tidak dihukum, maka keadilan TIDAK ADA. Faktanya KEADILAN itu ada, karena itu dosa harus dihukum.

Masalahnya manusia “menciptakan Tuhan” yang tidak adil (dalam pikirannya) sehingga menghasilkan Tuhan yang DAPAT menukar dosa dengan AMAL. Tuhan yang bisa menukar dosa dengan puasa. Tuhan yang bisa menukar kejahatan dengan perbuatan baik.

Saya tanya ketukang pangkas “apakah adil jika seorang hakim melepaskan penjahat hanya karena penjahat itu melakukan amal”. Dia jawab, TIDAK ADIL. Lalu saya tanya lagi, apakah kejahatan boleh dilepaskan dengan berpuasa? Keadilan dalam hatinya “bertubrukan” dengan ajaran yang ia pegang sehingga dia jawab “Tidak TAHU”.

Sebenarnya dia tahu jawabannya, namun karena imannya, akal sehatnya “mampet”, dia tidak jujur. Padahal jika dia jujur terhadap kebenaran, kebenaran itu akan membebaskannya dari ajaran yang ia pegang.

Ada tertulis “Dosa adalah pelanggaran terhadap hukum Allah”. Dosa berada di bawah tuntutan keadilan Allah. Karena keadilan Allah itu nyata, maka dosa harus dihukum. Dosa yang HANYA diampuni tanpa dihukum adalah KETIDAKADILAN. Ketidakadilan tanpa hukuman seperti ini adalah hayalan ala pengadilan bayaran.

Lalu bagaimana manusia bisa diselamatkan?
Jawaban satu-satunya adalah Yesus Kristus TELAH menanggung hukuman atas dosa Anda dan saya. Hukuman itu tidak dihapus, tetapi dipindahkan kepada Kristus, seperti ada tertulis:

a. Dia sendiri telah memikul dosa kita di dalam tubuhNya di kayu salib (1 Petrus 2:24).

b. Dia yang tidak mengenal dosa telah dibuatNya menjadi dosa karena kita, supaya dalam Dia kita dibenarkan oleh Allah (2 Korintus 5:21).

c. Kristus telah mati untuk dosa-dosa kita, sesuai dengan Kitab Suci (1 Korintus 15:3).

Di salib keadilan Allah tetap ditegakkan, karena dosa HARUS dihukum. Kasih Allah TELAH dinyatakan, karena Yesus MENANGGUNG hukuman itu bagi kita.

Itulah sebabnya Injil adalah kabar baik dari Surga. Manusia tidak DAPAT menyelamatkan dirinya dengan amal, puasa, atau perbuatan baik, tetapi oleh PENGORBANAN Yesus Kristus di salib.

Gbl. Ranto V. Simamora

articles.title: Karena kasih karunia kamu diselamatkan oleh iman!
articles.content:
Efesus 2:8-9 (TB) Sebab karena kasih karunia kamu diselamatkan oleh iman; itu bukan hasil usahamu, tetapi pemberian Allah, itu bukan hasil pekerjaanmu: jangan ada orang yang memegahkan diri.

Bagaimana dengan Yakobus 2:24 Jadi kamu lihat, bahwa manusia dibenarkan karena perbuatan-perbuatannya dan bukan hanya karena iman.

Perhatikan Yakobus memulainya dengan kesimpulan di ayat 17 bahwa iman yang benar harus DISERTAI perbuatan nyata. Perbuatan inilah yang menunjukkan, memperlihatkan iman kita tidak kosong apalagi mati, tapi iman yang benar dan hidup.

Yakobus 2:17 Demikian juga halnya dengan iman: Jika iman itu tidak disertai perbuatan, maka iman itu pada hakekatnya adalah mati.
18Tetapi mungkin ada orang berkata: ”Padamu ada iman dan padaku ada perbuatan”, aku akan menjawab dia: ”Tunjukkanlah kepadaku imanmu itu tanpa perbuatan, dan aku akan menunjukkan kepadamu imanku dari perbuatan-perbuatanku.” 19Engkau percaya, bahwa hanya ada satu Allah saja? Itu baik! Tetapi setan-setan pun juga percaya akan hal itu dan mereka gemetar. 20 Hai manusia yang bebal, maukah engkau mengakui sekarang, bahwa iman tanpa perbuatan adalah iman yang kosong? 21 Bukankah Abraham, bapa kita, dibenarkan karena perbuatan-perbuatannya, ketika ia mempersembahkan Ishak, anaknya, di atas mezbah? 22 Kamu lihat, bahwa iman bekerjasama dengan perbuatan-perbuatan dan oleh perbuatan-perbuatan itu iman menjadi sempurna. 23 Dengan jalan demikian genaplah nas yang mengatakan: “Lalu percayalah Abraham kepada Allah, maka Allah memperhitungkan hal itu kepadanya sebagai kebenaran.” Karena itu Abraham disebut: “Sahabat Allah.”

Roma 4:9 Adakah ucapan bahagia ini hanya berlaku bagi orang bersunat saja atau juga bagi orang tak bersunat? Sebab telah kami katakan, bahwa kepada Abraham iman diperhitungkan sebagai kebenaran. 10Dalam keadaan manakah hal itu diperhitungkan? Sebelum atau sesudah ia disunat? Bukan sesudah disunat, tetapi sebelumnya.

Perhatikan! Abraham dibenarkan SEBELUM dia melakukan perintah sunat! Tapi dia tetap melakukan sunat itu walaupun SUDAH dibenarkan.
Jadi tanpa perbuatan, iman itu cuman “ngomong doank,” “asal bunyi.”
Contoh misal saya dikasihtau, “jangan pegang, ini besi panas, nanti tanganmu terbakar,” lalu saya bilang “ya saya percaya,” tapi lalu saya pegang juga besi itu. Terlihat disini mulut saya bilang percaya tapi sebenarnya itu iman kosong, mati. Perbuatan saya itu menunjukkan iman saya kosong dan mati.

Roma 3:27-28 (TB) Jika demikian, apakah dasarnya untuk bermegah? Tidak ada! Berdasarkan apa? Berdasarkan perbuatan? Tidak, melainkan berdasarkan iman!
Karena kami yakin, bahwa manusia dibenarkan karena iman, dan bukan karena ia melakukan hukum Taurat.

Roma 4:3, 6, 10 (TB) Sebab apakah dikatakan nas Kitab Suci? “Lalu percayalah Abraham kepada Tuhan, dan Tuhan memperhitungkan hal itu kepadanya sebagai kebenaran.”
Seperti juga Daud menyebut berbahagia orang yang dibenarkan Allah bukan berdasarkan perbuatannya:
Dalam keadaan manakah hal itu diperhitungkan? Sebelum atau sesudah ia disunat? Bukan sesudah disunat, tetapi sebelumnya.

Roma 5:1 (TB) Sebab itu, kita yang dibenarkan karena iman, kita hidup dalam damai sejahtera dengan Allah oleh karena Tuhan kita, Yesus Kristus.

Roma 9:31-32 (TB) Tetapi: bahwa Israel, sungguhpun mengejar hukum yang akan mendatangkan kebenaran, tidaklah sampai kepada hukum itu. Mengapa tidak? Karena Israel mengejarnya bukan karena iman, tetapi karena perbuatan. Mereka tersandung pada batu sandungan,

Roma 10:9-10 (TB) Sebab jika kamu mengaku dengan mulutmu, bahwa Yesus adalah Tuhan, dan percaya dalam hatimu, bahwa Allah telah membangkitkan Dia dari antara orang mati, maka kamu akan diselamatkan. Karena dengan hati orang percaya dan dibenarkan, dan dengan mulut orang mengaku dan diselamatkan.

Roma 11:6 Tetapi jika hal itu terjadi karena kasih karunia, maka bukan lagi karena perbuatan, sebab jika tidak demikian, maka kasih karunia itu bukan lagi kasih karunia.

Galatia 2:16 (TB) Kamu tahu, bahwa tidak seorang pun yang dibenarkan oleh karena melakukan hukum Taurat, tetapi hanya oleh karena iman dalam Kristus Yesus. Sebab itu kami pun telah percaya kepada Kristus Yesus, supaya kami dibenarkan oleh karena iman dalam Kristus dan bukan oleh karena melakukan hukum Taurat. Sebab: “tidak ada seorang pun yang dibenarkan” oleh karena melakukan hukum Taurat.

Galatia 3:10-11 (TB) Karena semua orang, yang hidup dari pekerjaan hukum Taurat, berada di bawah kutuk. Sebab ada tertulis: “Terkutuklah orang yang tidak setia melakukan segala sesuatu yang tertulis dalam kitab hukum Taurat.”
Dan bahwa tidak ada orang yang dibenarkan di hadapan Allah karena melakukan hukum Taurat adalah jelas, karena: “Orang yang benar akan hidup oleh iman.”

2 Timotius 1:9
Dialah yang menyelamatkan kita dan memanggil kita dengan panggilan kudus, bukan berdasarkan perbuatan kita, melainkan berdasarkan maksud dan kasih karunia-Nya sendiri, yang telah dikaruniakan kepada kita dalam Kristus Yesus sebelum permulaan zaman

Titus 3:5
pada waktu itu Dia telah menyelamatkan kita, bukan karena perbuatan baik yang telah kita lakukan, tetapi karena rahmat-Nya oleh permandian kelahiran kembali dan oleh pembaharuan yang dikerjakan oleh Roh Kudus,

Tetaplah berpegang teguh pada iman yang menyelamatkan dan jangan pernah mundur meninggalkan iman yang benar ini.

Ibrani 10:38 (TB) Tetapi orang-Ku yang benar akan hidup oleh iman, dan apabila ia mengundurkan diri, maka Aku tidak berkenan kepadanya.”
